mutants.expected_detection: SR2 dead-time width check fails: for duty values 3..13, the observed dead-time gap becomes 1 cycle at the low-to-high boundary (cnt>=1 instead of cnt>=2) instead of the required 2 cycles, causing the testbench's exact dead-time run-length comparison against the reference to mismatch at the period-start boundary for every duty tested.

FR1 checks that for duty=8, en=1 held, pwm_hi asserts for exactly cnt=2..7 (6 cycles) and pwm_lo for cnt=10..15 (6 cycles) each 16-cycle period, matching the reference cycle-for-cycle over at least 4 periods. Swapping the stateA comparison operator from '<' to '<=' widens the pwm_hi window by one extra cycle (cnt=2..8 instead of 2..7 for duty=8), causing a mismatched cycle count against the reference and failing the cycle_accurate_match_rate / functional_equivalence metrics for FR1 (and also violating FR2/FR3 window-edge behavior).

FR2 sweep over duty=0..15 with en=1 held for 2+ periods will observe pwm_hi and pwm_lo simultaneously high (or mismatched vs reference) because stateB's guard condition is negated, causing the lo-side window to incorrectly include cycles that overlap the hi-side window (e.g. for mid-range duty values, stateB becomes true for cnt < duty+2 instead of cnt >= duty+2, which both breaks the FR2 no-overlap check and the FR1/FR3 waveform match).

FR3 check for duty=15 expects pwm_lo to never assert and pwm_hi to assert for cnt=2..14 (13 cycles); with duty_plus2 computed as duty+1 instead of duty+2, at duty=15 stateB becomes (cnt>=16) which is still always false (ok), but at duty=13 stateB now asserts one cycle early (cnt>=14 instead of cnt>=15), and critically for duty=14 stateB becomes (cnt>=15) instead of never asserting, causing pwm_lo to incorrectly assert at cnt=15 when duty=14, and shrinking dead time at the duty boundary for all mid-range duty values -- this also breaks the duty=0,1,2 and duty=15 boundary edge cases checked under FR3 since the hi/lo window edges shift by one cycle, producing mismatched cycle counts against the reference for the extreme duty values.

FR4 testbench deasserts en for at least 8 consecutive cycles and checks that pwm_hi/pwm_lo continue to update each cycle as a registered function of the held cnt/duty (matching the reference), rather than freezing. This mutant removes the counter's hold-on-!en branch, causing cnt to keep incrementing even when en=0. The counter therefore fails to hold, and the resulting pwm_hi/pwm_lo waveform diverges from the reference during the held interval, causing a cycle-accurate mismatch and FR4 failure.

The SR1 no-overlap check (asserting (pwm_hi & pwm_lo)==0 on every clock edge across the duty=0..15 sweep with randomized en toggling over at least 3 periods) will fire. By loosening stateB's lower guard from '>= duty+2' to '>= duty' (removing the two-count offset that separates the low-side window from the high-side window's closing boundary), stateB becomes true starting at cnt=duty, which is exactly the count at which stateA's own upper bound (cnt < duty) has just turned false the cycle before but where cnt=duty-1 (the last count where stateA is true) is immediately followed by cnt=duty where stateB now asserts one cycle later while pwm_hi is still registered high from the prior cycle's stateA=1 at cnt=duty-1, producing a directly observable cycle where pwm_hi(t+1) and pwm_lo(t+1) are simultaneously high (both registered outputs high on the same clock cycle) for duty values >=3, since stateA(cnt=duty-1)=1 and stateB(cnt=duty)=1 land on adjacent/overlapping registered cycles causing at least one cycle of true overlap during the sweep, immediately failing the harness's overlap invariant.
